Documentation/Doppio editor

Scene editor

Stable Doppio Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: windows/main.rs

The editing surface of Doppio: a scene tree, a rendered viewport, an inspector built from component cards, and a command history that every editing action records.

What the editor edits#

The editor reads and writes the same ECS scene data the runtime uses. A scene is a .caf file, and the project stores it under scenes/. The editor never owns a parallel scene format.

SurfaceWhat you can do
HierarchySearch, select, add and delete entities; expand parent groups; drag a row onto another to reparent it.
ViewportOrbit, pan and fly the camera; click to select; drag the move/rotate/scale gizmo; double-click to focus.
InspectorRename the entity, edit the combined transform, expand component cards, remove components and add behaviours.
AssetsBrowse the project, create/import assets, and pack a .cap.
ConsoleFiltered Errors, Log, Actions, Engine and UI entries.

Hierarchy#

  • Rows are built from Scene::Parent links, not a UI-only tree. Reordering or reparenting writes the ECS parent component, and the viewport resolves world transforms through the parent chain.
  • The search field filters by entity name. Parent groups compose position, rotation and scale into their children.
  • Every row and control has a stable id (hierarchy.list.entity_row.<n>, hierarchy.search, hierarchy.add), so flows and agents can target it.
  • The right-click menu adds, deletes and focuses an entity.

Inspector#

The inspector is composed from reusable cards:

Card Contents
Entity Name and identity, with a material chooser.
Transform Position, rotation and scale on one row set; values are bounded fields with drag and keyboard entry.
Component cards One collapsible card per component, with type-specific fields and a remove button.
Add Behaviour Opens the behaviour picker for components the engine exposes.

Colour fields use the colour picker, bounded numbers use sliders and numeric fields, and references use asset pickers with search. All edits publish a Message; none of the widgets call the engine directly.

Gizmos and scene markers#

The viewport overlays two components:

  • Transform gizmo — move (1), rotate (2) and scale (3) handles for the selected entity, with plane handles for move and a centre handle for uniform scale. Every drag is one undo step.
  • Scene markers — icons and frusta for lights, cameras, colliders and empties, which have no mesh to select. Markers sit under the gizmo in hit order: gizmo handle, then marker, then scene picking.

See Gizmos and markers for the full interaction model and screenshots.

Undo, redo and play mode#

  • Every editing command calls App::commit, recording one undo step. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z walk the history.
  • Scene → Play (Ctrl+Enter) ticks the engine. The status bar shows a Playing chip; play-mode changes are kept out of editor-only paths.
  • Scene → Save Scene (Ctrl+S) writes the .caf scene and updates the Saved badge.

Prefab palette#

Scene → Create Entity… (Ctrl+Shift+N) opens a built-in palette: mesh, point, directional and spot lights, camera, physics body, terrain, water, empty group and Duplicate Selection. The same palette is available from the Hierarchy +. Choosing an entry adds a configured entity; no plugin is required.

Empty and fixture states#

A new scene has no entity. With no engine session (for example a headless fixture), the viewport shows Waiting for the engine viewport… while the rest of the editor remains fully interactive. The scene3d fixture starts an engine-backed scene with lights, a camera and meshes for visual tests.
